speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help us understand your bleeding issues, can you tell me if you have a family history of bleeding disorders or if this bleeding has persisted for more than 24 hours since the extraction? Also, do you experience heavy menstrual periods if you are female?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling and easy bruising, I suspect a coagulation factor deficiency like Hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, and Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time (PT): 15 sec; Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT): 60 sec; Factor VIII and IX levels: Not provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT suggests a defect in the intrinsic pathway, but we need to distinguish between Hemophilia A and B. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX specific activity levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Factor VIII and IX levels effectively rule out Hemophilia A and B, pointing towards another intrinsic pathway defect like von Willebrand Disease or Factor XI deficiency. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor antigen and ristocetin cofactor activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since von Willebrand disease is ruled out, the next most likely cause for an isolated prolonged PTT in this context is Factor XI deficiency, especially given the joint swelling history. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI activity level.

speaker: Doctor
text: With Hemophilia A, B, and von Willebrand disease ruled out, I need to investigate other causes for the prolonged PTT and bleeding history. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI activity level and a mixing study.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal mixing study and Factor XI levels are confusing, but the family history of joint swelling strongly suggests a factor deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII inhibitor titer and repeat Factor VIII/IX levels with mixing study interpretation.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Factor VII, X, V, and II activity levels, as well as fibrinogen level.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor VII, X, V, and II activity levels: Not provided in data; Fibrinogen level: Not provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the persistent bleeding, easy bruising, and family history of joint swelling despite normal standard factor levels, I suspect a deficiency in Factor XII or a rare contact factor issue, though those don't typically cause bleeding. Let me request a comprehensive coagulation panel including Factor XI, VII, X, V, II, and fibrinogen levels, as well as a platelet function assay. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive coagulation panel including Factor XI, VII, X, V, II, fibrinogen, and platelet function assay.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor XI, VII, X, V, II, fibrinogen levels: Not provided in data; Platelet function assay: Not provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with normal standard factor levels and a family history of bleeding and joint swelling strongly suggests Hemophilia A or B, likely due to lab error or variant factors not initially captured. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A
